walkthroughs.body_html: Price level on y-axis, real GDP on x-axis. AD slopes down (price level up → real spending down). AS slopes up. Equilibrium where they cross. A rightward AD shift raises price level AND GDP — useful for inflation/growth analysis.
Fiscal: Treasury changes tax/spending — direct but slow. Monetary: Bank of England moves interest rates — fast but blunt. In a recession, expansionary fiscal (more G) + lower rates both boost AD.
Always evaluate: time lags, side-effects (e.g. inflation), magnitude (depends on multiplier), conflicts between objectives (growth vs inflation). Use 'however', 'depends on', 'in the long run'.
